title: Mapo Tofu
subtitle: Sichuan tofu in a spicy fermented black bean and chilli sauce
excerpt: The Sichuan classic: silken tofu simmered in a deeply savoury sauce of pork mince, doubanjiang, fermented black beans, and Sichuan pepper, producing the signature mala numbing heat. One of the most flavourful dishes in Chinese cooking.

recipe.sourceNotes: Mapo tofu (mápó dòufu, literally pockmarked old woman's tofu) is one of the most famous dishes of Sichuan cuisine and is attributed to a woman nicknamed Chen Mapo (Chen with the pockmarked face) who ran a restaurant in Chengdu in the late Qing dynasty. The dish is now made throughout China and the world. Its defining characteristics are the mala flavour profile (mala means numbing and spicy) produced by doubanjiang (Pixian bean paste), fermented black beans, and Sichuan pepper; and the characteristic silken tofu that is simmered in the sauce until it absorbs the flavour while staying tender. The oil that floats on the finished dish is traditional and desirable, not a sign of excess.

recipeTools.notes: A wok or deep frying pan.

content.text: Do not stir the tofu vigorously once it is in the sauce; gentle swirling of the pan keeps the cubes intact. Sichuan pepper should be toasted and ground just before use: pre-ground Sichuan pepper loses most of its numbing fragrance very quickly. The red oil floating on top is part of the dish. Serve with plain white rice to balance the heat.

items.preparation: Pixian-style fermented broad bean and chilli paste

content.text: Blanch the tofu cubes in lightly salted boiling water for 1 minute to firm slightly and season. Drain carefully. Heat the oil in a wok or pan over high heat until smoking. Add the pork mince and cook for 2 minutes, breaking it up, until browned. Add the doubanjiang and cook for 1 minute, stirring, until the oil turns red.

Add the garlic and ginger and cook for 30 seconds. Pour in the stock, add both soy sauces, and bring to a simmer. Gently slide the tofu cubes into the sauce. Simmer for 3 minutes, swirling the pan occasionally rather than stirring.

Stir the cornflour slurry and add it to the pan. Simmer for 1 to 2 minutes until the sauce thickens and coats the tofu. Drizzle with sesame oil, scatter with the ground Sichuan pepper and spring onion. Serve immediately with white rice.
